title: Bounce Back? Restitution Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A rubber ball bounces back high, a cricket ball bounces less, and a lump of dough just goes splat. Diya drops three balls from one metre onto the kitchen floor: they come back to 81 cm, 36 cm and zero. Can one number describe each bounce? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn the coefficient of restitution, e.

On a live motion notebook three balls are dropped from 1 m while the readout shows the speed in, the speed out and e, and a height vs time graph draws every bounce. A slow-mo replay freezes the rubber ball at the floor: 4.43 m/s in, 3.98 m/s out, e = 0.9. We prove step by step why each bounce height is e squared times the last, place e = 1 (elastic), e = 0 (perfectly inelastic) and everything between on one scale, compare a wall and two moving carts side by side, and solve a two-equation collision with momentum plus e. Then the exam trap (use relative speeds), an original JEE Main pattern question on the total distance of a bouncing ball, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
